notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR18: when the I-O phrase is specified and label records are present, "The labels are checked in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input-output label checking." and "The new labels are written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input-output label writing." Both steps are implementor-defined (§1985:C.2, item 61: "The labels are checked or written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input or output label handling."). The implementation's convention is that a file carries no label the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (§1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program"), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states the clause 'accepted-inert at 85'. The clause is parsed at 85 (FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format; VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses it from 2002, COBOL0902) and no binder, emitter or runtime member reads it, so the I-O arm of SequentialConnector.OpenCore opens the existing file for reading and writing and checks and writes no label, which is the whole of the convention. Probed at --std 85 on one host file: OPEN I-O answers 00 under LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD and under LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED, the READ and REWRITE that follow succeed, and the file holds the records alone before and after (no label bytes). The witness opens a LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD file I-O (status 00), reads its record, rewrites it and reads the new content back. Not covered by this verdict: the clause's own syntax is unchecked at 85 (kb/Work PB5070), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no entry for the label items of the 1985 implementor-defined list, so the convention is written down only in the VCR row.

next.reason: 1985: "When the I-O phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present... labels are checked"; 2023: "The 2023 OPEN general rules (14.9.27.4) state no label checking or writing; the LABEL RECORDS clause is no longer in the standard.". The 2023 OPEN rules cover I-O mode in full (GR 16) but nowhere check or write labels. The LABEL RECORDS clause this rule depends on is absent from 2023.
